subtitle: Mahmud Gawan and the Fall of Bahmani Justice

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a lone vizier before the crumbling silhouette of Bidar fort and a burning letter in the foreground
panels.action: Mahmud Gawan stands tall in court robes on the ramparts of Bidar, wind tugging his cloak, as a single parchment curls and blackens in unseen flame before him, the Deccan plateau stretching away under a stormy sky.

dialogue.text: In the high noon of the Bahmani kings, a Persian merchant named Mahmud Gawan ruled an empire with pen and measure—until one forged letter shattered both his life and their throne.

i18n.hi: बहमनी शौकत के दोपहर में, महमूद गवां नाम का फ़ारसी सौदागर कलम और नाप से राज चलाता रहा — जब तक एक झूठा ख़त उसकी ज़िंदगी और उनका तख़्त, दोनों न तोड़ गया।

panels.shot: medium-wide deck-level shot on a lateen-rigged ship rolling on the Arabian Sea, horizon low
panels.action: A young Mahmud Gawan in plain merchant’s robes grips the rail of a wooden ship, eyes set toward the hazy outline of the Konkan coast as waves slap the hull and gulls circle overhead.

dialogue.text: Around 1453, Mahmud of Gilan left the mist of the Caspian shores, not as a prince or general, but as a merchant-scholar sailing toward the Deccan’s rising Bahmani court.

i18n.hi: करीब 1453 में, गीलान का महमूद कास्पियन किनारों की धुंध छोड़कर, न शहज़ादा बनकर, न सिपहसलार, बल्कि सौदागर–अदीब बनकर दक्खन की उभरती बहमनी दरगाह की तरफ़ रवाना हुआ।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high balcony over Bidar, then down to an interior audience chamber
panels.action: Inside the hall at Bidar, under painted ceilings and hanging lamps, Mahmud Gawan bows before the Bahmani sultan, courtiers in rich turbans watching with a mix of curiosity and calculation.

dialogue.speaker: mahmud_gawan
dialogue.text: Majesty, I seek only to serve with ink, number and loyalty.

i18n.hi: जहाँपनाह, मैं बस स्याही, हिसाब और वफ़ादारी से ख़िदमत चाहता हूँ।

panels.shot: overhead map-table shot, hands arranging markers across a map of the Deccan
panels.action: Mahmud Gawan, now older and robed as a high official, leans over a large map of the Deccan, placing wooden markers along the Konkan and eastward routes while officers and scribes look on.

dialogue.text: Through the letters later gathered in Riyad-ul-Insha, his own words show how a foreign-born trader became wazir, guiding Bahmani arms from the Arabian Sea to the eastern plains.

i18n.hi: बाद में रियाज़-उल-इंशा में जमा उनके ख़त दिखाते हैं कि कैसे परदेसी सौदागर वज़ीर बना, बहमनी फ़ौजों को अरबी सागर से पूर्वी मैदानों तक राह दिखाते हुए।

panels.shot: dynamic coastal wide shot of troops and horses moving along surf-lined sands, fort in distance
panels.action: Armoured horsemen ride along a bright Konkan shore, waves hissing at their hooves, as Mahmud Gawan rides slightly apart, pointing toward the hill where Goa’s fort rises against the sky.

dialogue.text: Chroniclers like Ferishta remember him at the front of campaigns that carried Bahmani banners to Goa, binding the western sea-gates into the sultanate’s reach.

i18n.hi: फ़रिश्ता लिखता है, मुहिमों में वो खुद अगुवाई में था, जब बहमनी झंडे गोवा तक पहुँचे और पश्चिमी समुद्री बंदर बहमनी ज़द में आ गए।

panels.shot: mid-shot inside a crowded court, factions on either side, focus on Gawan calm at the center
panels.action: In the Bidar audience hall, Deccani nobles cluster on one side and foreign-born Afaqi nobles on the other, faces tense, while Mahmud Gawan stands between them, hands folded, calm but watchful.

dialogue.text: But beneath the carved rafters of Bidar, lines were hardening. Deccani nobles of long local standing eyed the Afaqi newcomers. Mahmud, a Persian, stood squarely in that contested space.

i18n.hi: लेकिन बीदर की नक्काशीदार छतों के नीचे लकीरें कड़ी हो रही थीं। पुराने देकनी उमरा अफ़ाक़ी नवआयदों को टेढ़ी नज़र से देखते थे। फ़ारसी महमूद ठीक उसी खींची हुई रेखा पर खड़ा था।

panels.shot: shadowed flashback tableau, slightly desaturated, distant and solemn
panels.action: In a dim recollection scene, armed men in turbans surround a group of dignified Persian sayyids in robes, their faces set with fear and defiance, as the backdrop shows the outline of Bidar’s walls.

dialogue.text: Ferishta recalls that even in 1446, before Gawan’s rise, factional fury had already spilled into violence, with Persian Shia sayyids massacred in Bidar’s struggle for influence.

i18n.hi: फ़रिश्ता याद करता है कि अभी 1446 में, गवां के उरूज़ से पहले ही, गिरोहों की दुश्मनी ख़ूनी हो चुकी थी, और बीदर की बादशाहत-कशी में फ़ारसी शिया सैयदों का क़त्ल-ए-आम हुआ।

panels.shot: top-down view of a parchment being inscribed with lines and numbers, Gawan’s hand steady
panels.action: Mahmud Gawan sits at a low desk, carefully drawing neat lines across a large parchment, columns of figures taking shape as officials bring in bundles of survey notes and land records.

dialogue.text: Against this backdrop he sought order. Eaton notes how Gawan expanded the sultanate’s tarafs from four to eight and launched systematic land measurement to steady revenue and curb arbitrary power.

i18n.hi: इसी माहौल में उसने क़ायदा तलाश किया। ईटन बताते हैं कि गवां ने सल्तनत के तरफ़ों को चार से बढ़ाकर आठ किया और बाक़ायदा ज़मीन नाप शुरू करवाई, जिससे ख़ज़ाना संभले और मनमानी ताक़त कटी।

panels.shot: architectural hero wide of the Mahmud Gawan Madrasa facade in bright daylight
panels.action: Mahmud Gawan stands in the courtyard of his new madrasa at Bidar, its tall facade dressed in glazed tiles and arches, students and teachers moving under domed halls and shaded colonnades.

dialogue.text: By 876 AH, 1471–72 CE, an inscription named him founder of a grand madrasa at Bidar, its domes, tilework and library proclaiming the wazir’s ambition to bind learning to power.

i18n.hi: 876 हिजरी, 1471–72 में, एक क़िला-नवीस उसे बीदर की शानदार मदरसा का बानी कहता है — जिसके गुम्बद, चीनी-फ़रश और किताबख़ाना दिखाते हैं कि वज़ीर इल्म को ताक़त से बाँधना चाहता था।

panels.shot: intimate medium of Gawan seated among students and books, light slanting in
panels.action: Inside a cool hall lined with niches of books, Mahmud Gawan sits on a simple cushion, a manuscript open before him, as young pupils listen while scribes copy texts at low desks.

dialogue.speaker: mahmud_gawan
dialogue.text: An empire that forgets its books soon forgets its borders.

i18n.hi: जो सल्तनत किताबें छोड़ दे, वो सरहदें भी भूल जाती है।

panels.shot: wide of council chamber, with boundary map on wall and nobles reacting uneasily
panels.action: In a council chamber, Mahmud Gawan points to a detailed map of the eight tarafs, lines clearly marked, while a few Deccani nobles exchange dark, unsettled glances behind him.

dialogue.text: Yet every reform drew new lines. His measured assessments and province divisions strengthened the crown—but also cut into old patronage, deepening resentments already sharpened by origins and faith.

i18n.hi: पर हर इस्लाह ने नई रेखाएँ खींचीं। उसकी नाप-तोल की लगान और सूबों की तक़सीम ने ताज को मज़बूत किया — मगर पुराने ओढ़े-बिछोने काट दिए, और नस्ली व मज़हबी रंजिशें और गहरी हो गईं।

panels.shot: tight two-shot of whispering nobles in a shadowed arcade, Gawan blurred in background
panels.action: In a shadowed arcade of the palace, two nobles whisper close, eyes narrowed toward the distant figure of Mahmud Gawan speaking with a scribe in the sunlit courtyard beyond.

dialogue.text: Chroniclers describe Deccani-Afaqi rivalry coiling around him. To some, the foreign-born wazir seemed too powerful, too trusted, his scales of justice tilting the balance of the realm.

i18n.hi: तारीख़-निगार लिखते हैं कि देकनी–अफ़ाक़ी दुश्मनी उसी को घेरे घूमती थी। कुछ के लिए ये परदेसी वज़ीर हद से ज़्यादा ताक़तवर, हद से ज़्यादा भरोसेमंद लगा, जिसकी तराज़ू न्याय से ज़्यादा सल्तनत का पलड़ा झुका देती थी।

panels.shot: close-up on a hand forging a letter by lamplight, with seal impressions nearby
panels.action: Under the glow of an oil lamp, a hand carefully traces Arabic script on thick paper, then presses an official-looking seal beside other impressions laid out on the writing board.

dialogue.text: At some point, in this world of ink and intrigue, a letter was forged. Ferishta tells of a document crafted to make Mahmud Gawan appear a traitor to the very crown he served.

i18n.hi: यहीं कहीं, इस स्याही और साज़िश की दुनिया में, एक ख़त गढ़ा गया। फ़रिश्ता एक ऐसे दस्तावेज़ का ज़िक्र करता है जिसे इस तरह लिखा गया कि महमूद गवां ही ताज का गद्दार लगे।

panels.shot: medium in the throne room as the Sultan reads the letter, Gawan framed at a distance
panels.action: In the throne hall, the Bahmani sultan sits rigid on the dais, eyes scanning a letter held in his hand, while Mahmud Gawan stands below, face unreadable, the court’s gaze fixed on him.

dialogue.text: One day in 1481, that paper reached the king. The same court that had once cheered the merchant from Gilan now held its breath as suspicion took the place of trust.

i18n.hi: 1481 के एक दिन, वही काग़ज़ बादशाह की नज़र से गुज़रा। वही दरबार जिसने गीलान के सौदागर पर कभी तालियाँ बजाईं थीं, अब शक के साये में साँसें रोककर खड़ा था।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Gawan’s composed face, eyes steady, shadows deep
panels.action: Mahmud Gawan’s face fills the frame, lines of age and long work etched deep, his gaze steady but tired, a faint light catching the edge of his turban in the dim hall.

dialogue.speaker: mahmud_gawan
dialogue.text: My lord, I ask only that you weigh my deeds against this ink.

i18n.hi: आका, बस मेरे कामों को इस स्याही से तौल लीजिए।

panels.shot: somber wide shot of a courtyard at dusk with Gawan being led away under guard
panels.action: At dusk in a quiet courtyard, Mahmud Gawan walks with measured steps between two guards, his hands free but his fate clear, as the walls of Bidar loom in cool blue shadow.

dialogue.text: According to Ferishta, there was no long inquiry. The forged charge was enough. In that year, the Bahmani state cut down its own chief architect of order.

i18n.hi: फ़रिश्ता के मुताबिक़, कोई लम्बी तहक़ीक़ात न हुई। वही झूठा इल्ज़ाम काफी साबित हुआ। उसी साल बहमनी हुकूमत ने अपने ही सबसे बड़े मुनज़्ज़िम का सर कलम कर दिया।

panels.shot: poignant medium of the madrasa courtyard empty at night, Gawan’s discarded turban band in foreground
panels.action: Under a starry night, the cloistered courtyard of the Bidar madrasa lies silent, a single lamp burning by an arch, while a folded strip of cloth, like a turban band, rests abandoned on the stone.

dialogue.text: His madrasa remained, its halls still echoing with recitation, but its founder was gone. A crown that had trusted a forged letter more than a lifetime’s service had broken its own spine.

i18n.hi: मदरसा तो रहा, उसके दालान आज भी तिलावत से गूँजते रहे, पर उसका बानी चला गया। जिस ताज ने एक झूठे ख़त पर, उम्र भर की ख़िदमत से ज़्यादा भरोसा किया, उसने अपना ही मेरूदंड तोड़ दिया।

panels.shot: high aerial of the Deccan plateau with later Deccan sultanate capitals marked by their skylines
panels.action: From high above the Deccan plateau, the viewer sees distant silhouettes of Gulbarga, Bidar and the later Deccan capitals on different horizons, hazed by dust and distance under a pale sky.

dialogue.text: In the years after 1481, the Bahmani realm splintered into new Deccan sultanates. Eaton notes how Gawan’s death marked a turning, when factional mistrust began to pull the empire apart.

i18n.hi: 1481 के बाद के बरसों में बहमनी सल्तनत टूटकर नए दक्खनी सुल्तानतों में बिखर गई। ईटन बताते हैं कि गवां की मौत ही वो मोड़ थी, जहाँ से गुटबाज़ी की बेइत्तमादी ने सल्तनत की जड़ें उखाड़नी शुरू कर दीं।

panels.shot: present-day style wide of the ruined madrasa facade, ghostly overlay of Gawan’s figure
panels.action: In the present, the weathered ruins of the Mahmud Gawan Madrasa rise under a clear Deccan sun, while a faint, transparent image of Mahmud Gawan seems to stand in its courtyard, watching in silence.

dialogue.text: Today his tiled walls still stand in Bidar, a reminder that an empire can be measured, mapped and schooled to greatness—yet fall in an instant when envy is allowed to forge the truth.

i18n.hi: आज भी बीदर में उसकी चीनी-फ़रश दीवारें खड़ी हैं — याद दिलाती हैं कि सल्तनत नापी, नक़्शे में ढाली और मदरसे से ऊँची की जा सकती है, पर एक पल की हसरत, जब झूठ गढ़ने लगे, उसे धराशायी भी कर देती है।

title_i18n.en: The Merchant Who Governed an Empire
title_i18n.hi: वो सौदागर जिसने एक साम्राज्य चलाया

subtitle_i18n.en: Mahmud Gawan and the Fall of Bahmani Justice
subtitle_i18n.hi: महमूद गवां और बहमनी इंसाफ का पतन
